request.spec:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

agent.result_text:
Transferring a person to a sheet where someone already has the same name or alias now merges them into that person instead of being refused. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

The whole change is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/person/PersonTransferService.java`; no front-end or schema changes were needed.

**What happens on a match:**
- Names and aliases are compared the existing way: trimmed and ignoring case.
- The arriving person's claims go to the matching person and are listed after that person's own claims. They take the other sheet's next numbers, the same as any transfer, and any figures a statement had bound are released.
- The arriving person's name and aliases are added to the matching person's aliases. In the test, Ada ends up with "Ad, Addie, addie".
- The other sheet's audit file gets `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … name=<name> from=<sheet id>`, then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, then the usual rollup lines.

**Edge cases the request didn't spell out.** These are my own calls, and the test doesn't exercise them:
- **Still refused:** the names match more than one person, or match someone on a sheet below the other sheet rather than on that sheet itself.
- **Refused:** the matching person is retired, because a normal merge refuses retired people.
- **Contact:** on a merge the "contact already in use" check is skipped and the arriving person's contact is dropped, as a normal merge drops it. With no match, that check still applies.
- **Dropped:** the arriving person's statements, holds, patron links, pool memberships and watches are dropped, as a normal transfer already does. Unlike an in-sheet merge, their patron links and pool memberships aren't carried over to the matching person.
